# Methods

## Ethics approval

The study was approved by the ethics committee of the University Medicine Greifswald
(reference number: `r rmarkdown::metadata[["ethics_committee"]][["reference_number"]]`;
approval date: `r rmarkdown::metadata[["ethics_committee"]][["approval_date"]]`).
It was registered on 26 April 2024 at the Open Science Framework
(https://osf.io/5bmj8).
We did not collect, store, share, or publish
any directly or indirectly identifiable patient data.
Therefore, informed consent and a data protection declaration were not required.

## Definitions

Following the taxonomy introduced by Gandhi et al.,
*capture efficiency* refers to the entire recapture process
and is defined as the ratio of the total mass of sevoflurane
recovered from the canisters to the total mass administered.
*In vivo mass transfer* describes the increase in canister mass
relative to the mass of volatile anaesthetic used during clinical cases [@Gandhi2024].

## Setting

This pragmatic, prospective, multicentre observational study was conducted from
`r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[1L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
to
`r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[2L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
across `r n_center["initial"]` hospitals in Germany and Austria,
encompassing `r n_ors["initial"]` operating rooms (ORs).

The duration of the study in each participating OR was determined by the consecutive usage of
`r n_bottles_per_or` bottles of sevoflurane
(`r sevo_bottle_ml` ml, `r sevo_g_per_bottle` g each).
Before the first anaesthesia,
the vaporizer was filled to the maximum from a non-study bottle to standardise
the initial conditions.
The study ended
when the last study bottle had been emptied into the vaporizer.
Sevoflurane was the only permitted volatile anaesthetic in the study ORs.
In each OR,
a CONTRAfluran activated charcoal canister (ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Luckenwalde, Germany)
was installed at the exhaust port of the anaesthesia machine
to passively capture sevoflurane during inhalational anaesthesia.
The canister was not connected to the anaesthesia gas scavenging system.
Canisters were replaced when the red LED on the SENSOfluran unit
(ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Luckenwalde, Germany) indicated saturation.
At the end of the study the canister in use was disconnected
regardless of its saturation level.
All anaesthesia cases were managed at the discretion of the attending
anaesthesiologist.

Case-level data were collected prospectively by the attending anaesthesiologist
using a structured paper-based case report form (CRF).
For each anaesthesia case, the CRF recorded
start and end times,
whether inhalational anaesthesia was used,
airway device (laryngeal mask or tracheal tube),
type of surgical approach (laparoscopic or non-laparoscopic),
fresh gas flow 15 minutes after induction,
and the sequential numbers of canister and sevoflurane bottle in use.
Regional anaesthesia cases without airway management and without connection
to the anaesthesia machine were excluded.
Cases with missing information on these informations were retained in the overall case count
for the respective canister but were excluded from the corresponding subgroup analyses.
After study completion, the CRFs were returned to the coordinating study
centre as scanned copies via e-mail for central data entry.

## Outcome

The primary outcome was the capture efficiency of the CONTRAfluran canisters
defined as the ratio of the mass of sevoflurane recovered by ZeoSys
to the mass of sevoflurane attributable to the analysed canisters.
Sevoflurane use was estimated from the `r sevo_bottle_ml` ml bottles used per OR
and allocated to canisters as described below.

## Weight measurement and consumption estimation

Weight gain per canister represents the *in vivo* mass transfer.
It was calculated as the difference between
the median unsaturated weight of the corresponding canister type and
the pre-desorption weight recorded at the ZeoSys manufacturing facility in
Luckenwalde, Germany.

Some canisters were weighed twice at ZeoSys prior to desorption
(`r zeosys_storage_days` days apart).
The difference between the two weighings was used to estimate weight loss during storage
(Online Supplementary Figure\ \@ref(fig:weight-loss-storage-plot)).
Because not all canisters were available for the first weighing,
weight gain was calculated from the second, more complete weighing.

The CONTRAfluran canisters were obtained from ZeoSys
by each participating centre individually.
During the study period the canister design was modified.
In comparison to the previous generation with a batch number starting with CH, the recent
canisters with a batch number starting with CN had a different lid with a 30 mm female instead of a 20
mm male connector to avoid incorrect connection to the airway system.
To determine the unsaturated weight,
the median unsaturated weight of
`r baseline_weights$n[baseline_weights$type == "CH"]` CH-canisters from our previous
study [@Gibb2025] was used,
and another
`r baseline_weights$n[baseline_weights$type == "CN"]` CN-canisters were weighed.
The median unsaturated weight was
`r round(baseline_weights$median[baseline_weights$type == "CH"], 1)` g
(IQR `r round(baseline_weights$iqr[baseline_weights$type == "CH"], 1)` g)
for CH-type canisters and
`r round(baseline_weights$median[baseline_weights$type == "CN"], 1)` g
(IQR `r round(baseline_weights$iqr[baseline_weights$type == "CN"], 1)` g)
for CN-type canisters.

As sevoflurane use was recorded per OR
and not per canister,
the total amount of sevoflurane used in each OR (`r n_bottles_per_or` bottles)
was allocated proportionally across its canisters based on the median
fresh gas flow recorded 15 minutes after induction across all cases using that
canister multiplied by the total anaesthesia duration of that canister.

## Batch assignment for thermal desorption

The study protocol originally specified desorption in batches of 20 canisters.
At the time of desorption, routine processing at ZeoSys required
a batch size of 80 canisters.
Accordingly, 80 of the `r n_eligible` eligible canisters were selected
for desorption in a single batch.

Cases were classified by airway device (laryngeal mask vs. tracheal tube),
surgical approach (laparoscopic vs. non-laparoscopic),
and anaesthetic technique (inhalational anaesthesia vs. total intravenous
anaesthesia, TIVA).
As no laparoscopic case was performed with a laryngeal mask,
six combinations remained.
For each combination, three variables were derived:
number of cases, cumulative anaesthesia duration,
and the median of the recorded fresh gas flows,
yielding `r length(clustering_columns) - 1L` variables.
Where a canister had no cases in a given combination,
all three variables were set to zero,
including the median fresh gas flow.
Water trap use between the anaesthesia machine and the canister
was added as a binary variable,
giving `r length(clustering_columns)` variables.
The assignment was based solely on the variables described above,
not on weight or desorption data.

All `r length(clustering_columns)` variables were scaled to zero mean and unit variance.
A batch of 80 canisters was selected using fixed-size nearest-neighbour clustering.
The canister with the smallest sum of Euclidean distances to all other canisters was identified,
and its `r n_agcs["final"] - 1L` nearest neighbours were selected.

The study protocol originally specified Ward’s minimum variance method.
The requirement to select exactly 80 of the `r n_eligible` eligible canisters,
excluding the remaining `r fmt_count(n_excl_outlier)`,
necessitated a fixed-size clustering approach,
as Ward’s method does not allow direct specification of cluster size.

The protocol had originally specified Ward's minimum variance method for this grouping,
which cannot be constrained to a fixed group size.
Applied to the same distances,
Ward's method yielded a higher within-cluster sum of squares
than the selection used here.
The batch size and the clustering method both deviated from the study protocol.

## Statistical analysis

All data processing and statistical analyses were performed using R version
`r paste0(sessionInfo()$R.version[c("major", "minor")], collapse = ".")`
[@R-base].
The data generated and analysed in this study
and the code that produced the results reported here
are available at https://github.com/umg-minai/vct-or-mc [@vctormcdata].
